thread:
alice: customer (Acme Inc) reporting intermittent 401s and a sudden billing spike during our new canary for redwood-v2-300m. They say requests sometimes succeed, sometimes 401. Can we collect repro steps + debug bundle?
ben: which region, time window, and any request-ids we have?
alice: region=us-west-2, window=2026-03-15T14:02:00Z - 14:20:00Z. Got these request ids from the customer: rq_8f3a2c, rq_8f3a96, rq_8f3b10.
carla: can you ask them to run a curl reproducer? give them this exact command but tell them to replace $TOKEN: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v2-300m","input":"test repro"}' \
  https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate
```
dan: also ask them to include the header X-Debug: full so we can capture gateway trace.
alice: posted the curl output from customer (redacted token): 
```
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood-inference.com
> Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
< content-type: application/json
< x-request-id: rq_8f3a96
{
  "error": "invalid_api_key",
  "message": "token expired"
}
```
ben: token expired could be a client issue but intermittent success suggests maybe routing to a backend that validates differently (canary vs stable). Did the customer hit the same model endpoint when it succeeded?
alice: they said success usually goes to redwood-v2-300m@stable, failures to redwood-v2-300m@canary (they snooped via our model header).
carla: that points to rollout policy mismatch — canary might be using a different auth check path if deployed to a private pool or different gateway. infra-bot: created debug bundle 1764032100-acme-123.tar.gz and uploaded to internal S3: https://s3.redwood-internal/debug-bundles/1764032100-acme-123.tar.gz :thumbsup:
ben: grabbing gateway logs for rq_8f3a96 and nearby timestamps now. If we can get the customer's full HTTP request (headers) that helps.
dan: check for clock skew on their client causing jwt "exp" to be in the past for some requests. Also check our auth service logs for token validation errors.
alice: attached masked client request headers from customer (they removed token): 
```
Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>
User-Agent: acme-sync/2.1
X-Client-Time: 2026-03-15T14:05:12Z
X-Debug: full
```
ben: gateway log excerpt for rq_8f3a96: 
```
[2026-03-15T14:05:12.345Z] INFO request_id=rq_8f3a96 route=/v1/generate model=redwood-v2-300m variant=canary auth_status=invalid_api_key detail="token expired"
[2026-03-15T14:05:12.346Z] DEBUG upstream=auth-svc response=401 jwt_exp=2026-03-15T14:05:10Z
```
carla: jwt_exp shows token expired by 2s. If their clock lags a little that can flip. But why stable requests succeed? Maybe stable route has a slightly different auth cache TTL or revalidate path.
dan: quick repro steps for customer: 1) capture token generation time and exp, 2) run curl with same token and X-Debug header, 3) paste full response headers. I can provide a tiny script to loop and surface failure rate.
carla: another angle — if canary is on a different datacenter, time sync might differ slightly due to ntp drift on that host pool. We should check canary pool NTP status.
ben: I pulled host NTP check for canary pool — last sync 2026-03-15T13:58:00Z (ok). But auth-svc instances in that pool show a 1-2s drift in logs. I'll open infra ticket.
alice: customer also saw a billing jump. They said ~x10 token count while retries happened. Could be client retrying on 401 and getting charged. Need to recommend temporary mitigation.
dan: mitigation: pin them to stable model until we fix. Example header to pin: 
```
Model-Pin: redwood-v2-300m@stable
```
or include in request body: {"model":"redwood-v2-300m@stable"}. That will bypass canary routing.
carla: recommend adding explicit fallback policy on rollout so 401s don't trigger charged retries — e.g., fallback to stable on auth failures. We should also ensure gateway returns 429 or 503 for transient infra errors, not 401.
alice: I told customer to pin to stable for now, run the curl we sent and upload the debug bundle we provided. They uploaded bundle and I linked it above.
deploy-bot: canary deployment redwood-v2-300m started 2026-03-15T13:50Z (id: deploy_9821). Rolling to 20% traffic.
ben: next actions: (1) SRE check auth-svc time sync and token validation path for canary pool, (2) Product add rollout fallback rule for auth failures, (3) Support provide customer repro curl and confirm pin-to-stable worked. I'll own 1.
carla: I'll draft rollout policy change and toy up a regression test for auth validation differences.
dan: I'll share a small script for the customer to run repeated requests and capture success/fail rates.
alice: thanks all — customer on call at 16:00 PT. Will ask them to run curl+script and confirm pin. Will update thread after call. :pray:
